step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 25-year-old male shrimp farm worker presenting with acute gastroenteritis after mollusc ingestion

step5_concept_grounding: Non-O1/non-O139 Vibrio cholerae gastroenteritis; non-toxigenic isolate lacking cholera toxin genes

evidence_items.source_quote: Stool culture was spread onto Thiosulfate-citrate-bile salts-sucrose (TCBS) and MacConkey agar plates, which gave suspected positive results for V. cholerae.
evidence_items.test_name: Stool culture on TCBS and MacConkey

evidence_items.source_quote: Agglutination with O1 and O139 antisera showed that this strain was a non-O1/O139 V. cholerae.
evidence_items.test_name: Slide agglutination with O1 and O139 antisera

evidence_items.source_quote: Genomic analysis showed that all V. cholerae isolates found in this study were positive for toxR gene, but negative for zot, ctxA, hlyA, tcpA, tcpI, and ompU genes.
evidence_items.test_name: Whole-genome and PCR virulence gene profiling

rationale: A 25-year-old male presented with watery diarrhea and vomiting following raw mollusc ingestion. Stool culture on TCBS isolated Vibrio cholerae, but slide agglutination with O1 and O139 antisera was negative, and genomic analysis confirmed absence of cholera toxin genes (ctxA, zot, tcpA). Non-O1/non-O139 V. cholerae intestinal infection represents non-target vibriosis rather than epidemic cholera. VPD not satisfied -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 54-year-old diabetic male with severe bacteremic right lower limb cellulitis and gangrene

step5_concept_grounding: Non-O1/non-O139 Vibrio cholerae soft tissue infection and bacteremia, not clinical cholera

evidence_items.source_quote: The initial blood culture taken on 27/07/2018 flagged positive for Vibrio cholerae after 8.5 h of incubation in the BACT/ALERT  VIRTUO  (bioMerieux, US).
Manual testing confirmed it showing it as Non O1, Non O139 serotype.

rationale: A 54-year-old diabetic male presented with right lower extremity cellulitis and impending sepsis. Blood culture isolated non-O1, non-O139 Vibrio cholerae. The patient had bacteremic soft tissue infection/gangrene rather than clinical cholera (acute diarrheal illness caused by toxigenic V. cholerae). VPD not satisfied -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 51-year-old male with esophageal cancer presenting with oral mucosal pseudomembranous infection

step5_concept_grounding: Non-O1/non-O139 Vibrio cholerae oral stomatitis/mucositis, not clinical cholera

evidence_items.source_quote: Oral swab samples were collected for culture. After 24 h of incubation, beta-hemolytic, oxidase-positive colonies grew on blood agar. On thiosulfate-citrate-bile salts-sucrose agar, the organism appeared as large, yellow colonies. V. cholerae was suspected and identified by the Bruker Biotyper MALDI-TOF MS system, which showed identification log scores of 2.151 (>2.0 is considered reliable for species identification). V. cholerae failed to agglutinate with O1 and O139 antisera.
evidence_items.test_name: Oral swab culture and MALDI-TOF with serotyping

evidence_items.source_quote: V. cholerae was not isolated from his stool specimen.

rationale: A 51-year-old male undergoing chemoradiotherapy for esophageal cancer presented with pseudomembranous oral stomatitis. Oral swab cultures grew non-O1/non-O139 Vibrio cholerae lacking cholera toxin genes, while stool culture was negative. The patient had an opportunistic oral mucosal infection, not cholera. VPD not satisfied -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 73-year-old female presenting with necrotizing fasciitis of the left lower leg after pond exposure

step5_concept_grounding: Non-O1/non-O139 Vibrio cholerae necrotizing soft-tissue wound infection; stool negative; not clinical cholera

evidence_items.source_quote: Necrotizing fasciitis was diagnosed and swabs gained intraoperatively yielded non-O1/non-O139 V. cholerae (bacteriological results reported on day 7).
A stool sample on day 7 was negative for V. cholerae.

rationale: A 73-year-old female developed severe necrotizing fasciitis of the lower leg requiring urgent fasciotomy after swimming in an Austrian bathing pond. Intraoperative wound swabs isolated non-O1/non-O139 Vibrio cholerae, whereas stool testing was negative for V. cholerae. The patient suffered an extraintestinal necrotizing soft-tissue infection, not the clinical entity of cholera. VPD not satisfied -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: An 80-year-old male presenting with necrotizing fasciitis of the left lower leg and septic shock

step5_concept_grounding: Non-O1/non-O139 Vibrio cholerae necrotizing fasciitis and septic shock after swimming exposure

evidence_items.source_quote: Blood cultures taken on day 2 yielded V. cholerae (bacteriological results reported on day 5).

On day 3, bilateral fasciotomy and debridement were performed on his left lower leg and necrotizing fasciitis was diagnosed; swabs taken intraoperatively yielded growth of non-O1/non-O139 V. cholerae.

rationale: An 80-year-old male developed severe necrotizing fasciitis of the lower extremity and septic shock following swimming in an Austrian pond. Blood cultures and intraoperative wound swabs isolated nontoxigenic non-O1/non-O139 Vibrio cholerae lacking ctxA/ctxB. The condition was an invasive aquatic soft-tissue infection and sepsis, not the clinical entity of cholera. VPD not satisfied -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 47-year-old female lung transplant recipient presenting with severe watery and bloody diarrhea and orthostasis

step5_concept_grounding: Non-O1, non-O139 Vibrio cholerae diarrheal infection in an immunocompromised host, distinct from epidemic cholera

evidence_items.source_quote: Six hours later, while being wheeled to the endoscopy suite for EGD at our institution, the laboratory called to report positive V. cholerae culture results from a stool sample (Figure 1).

The patient's antibiotics were switched to cover this microorganism. After a single dose of doxycycline, the symptoms of orthostasis and dysentery resolved with a dramatic improvement in overall status.

rationale: A 47-year-old female lung transplant recipient developed severe watery/bloody diarrhea and orthostasis after consuming seafood. Stool culture isolated Vibrio cholerae identified as a non-O1, non-O139 strain. Non-O1/non-O139 V. cholerae gastroenteritis represents non-cholera vibriosis rather than epidemic cholera. VPD not satisfied -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 54-year-old male with multiple myeloma presenting with septic shock and fatal hemorrhagic complications

step5_concept_grounding: Non-O1/non-O139 Vibrio cholerae septicemia in an immunosuppressed host; non-target strain, not epidemic cholera

evidence_items.source_quote: Blood culture identification showed growth of Vibrio cholerae non-O1/non-O139.

rationale: A 54-year-old male with multiple myeloma developed fatal septic shock after travel to Haiti. Blood cultures isolated non-O1/non-O139 Vibrio cholerae. Non-O1/non-O139 bacteremia represents opportunistic invasive vibriosis rather than epidemic cholera. VPD not satisfied -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 64-year-old female with cirrhosis presenting with community-acquired pneumonia and pleural effusion

step5_concept_grounding: Vibrio albensis bacteremia and pneumonia, not Vibrio cholerae or cholera

evidence_items.source_quote: The organism was identified as vibrio albensis by the mass spectrometry assisted by flight time desorption/ionization matrix (MALDI TOF-MS, Billerica, MA, USA), with a 99% confidence level.
evidence_items.test_name: Blood culture with MALDI-TOF MS identification

evidence_items.source_quote: The antimicrobial susceptibility of this strain was tested based on the CDC recommendation for V. cholerae and an extended battery of other antimicrobials using disk diffusion tests and interpreted according to the Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute guideline (CLASI)

rationale: A 64-year-old female with liver cirrhosis presented with pneumonia and bacteremia. Blood culture identified Vibrio albensis by MALDI-TOF, with V. cholerae mentioned purely as an interpretive testing reference standard. The infection was caused by Vibrio albensis, not Vibrio cholerae or cholera. VPD not satisfied -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 70-year-old male returned traveler from Senegal presenting with fever, liver abscesses, and bacteremia

step5_concept_grounding: Non-O1, non-O139 Vibrio cholerae bacteremia with hepatic abscesses; toxigenic cholera ruled out

evidence_items.source_quote: One of the two sets of blood cultures collected upon admission yielded a Gram-negative rod, compatible with V. cholerae (Fig. 2). Stool cultures were negative.
evidence_items.target_concept: Vibrio cholerae bacteremia with negative stool culture

evidence_items.source_quote: The strain did not agglutinate when tested against O1 or O139 antisera. PCR techniques demonstrated the absence of the major virulence-encoding genes of toxigenic V. cholerae, the cholera-toxin (ctxA and ctxB) and the toxin-coregulated pilus (tcpA) virulence genes, and of the stn gene, encoding a heat-stable enterotoxin reported to contribute to the pathogenicity of NOVC.
evidence_items.test_name: National Reference Center seroagglutination and virulence PCR
evidence_items.target_concept: O1/O139 agglutination and cholera toxin (ctxA, ctxB)

step10_contradiction_notes: Suspicion of cholera or toxigenic V. cholerae ruled out by negative stool culture, negative O1/O139 seroagglutination, and negative cholera toxin PCR (ctxA/ctxB).
rationale: A 70-year-old male returned from Senegal with watery diarrhea, fever, and liver abscesses. Blood culture grew Vibrio cholerae, but evaluation at the National Reference Center proved negative for O1 and O139 antisera, negative for cholera toxin genes (ctxA/ctxB), and stool cultures were negative. Cholera was definitively tested and ruled out, and the patient was diagnosed with non-O1/non-O139 pyogenic liver abscess and bacteremia. VPD not satisfied -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 27-year-old male with recurrent right-ear otitis media after eardrum perforation during water skiing

step5_concept_grounding: Vibrio cholerae serogroup O100 otitis media, not clinical cholera

evidence_items.source_quote: A 27-years old Caucasian male with acute otitis media presented to an otolaryngologist at a medical clinic in Haifa, Israel, after suffering for a period of three years from a periodic earache accompanied by a malodorous and purulent exudate from his right ear, without fever.

The isolate was confirmed as V. cholerae non-O1/O139, cholera toxin-negative by the reference laboratory of the Israeli Ministry of Health. Somatic antigen serogrouping identification was employed on the five V. cholerae isolates according to, and all the isolates were identified as V. cholerae serogroup O100.
evidence_items.test_name: Reference laboratory serogrouping and toxin PCR
evidence_items.target_concept: V. cholerae serogroup O100 non-O1/O139, cholera toxin-negative

rationale: A 27-year-old male presented with chronic purulent otitis media after eardrum perforation during water skiing. Ear exudate culture identified non-O1/non-O139 Vibrio cholerae serogroup O100 lacking cholera toxin. The clinical disease is an extraintestinal ear infection, not the diarrheal disease cholera. VPD not satisfied -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 27-year-old male presenting with acute dysuria and urinary tract infection following beach swimming

step5_concept_grounding: Non-O1/non-O139 Vibrio cholerae urinary tract infection; extraintestinal presentation, not clinical cholera

evidence_items.source_quote: A 27-year-old Saudi male from Al-Khobar City in the Eastern Province of Saudi Arabia presented to the emergency department at King Fahd Hospital of the University (KFHU) on 17th July 2021 with burning micturition.

The serological of isolate was determined by slide agglutination test using V. cholerae O1 and V. cholerae O139 polyvalent antisera (MAST ASSURE Antiserum Vibrio cholerae polyvalent, UK). The isolate gave a negative result with both polyvalent antiserum and reported as non-O1/non-O139 V. cholerae strain according to the manufacturer's instruction.
evidence_items.test_name: Urine culture slide agglutination with O1/O139 antisera

rationale: A 27-year-old male presented with dysuria following marine exposure. Urine culture isolated non-O1/non-O139 Vibrio cholerae. The patient presented with a localized urinary tract infection without gastrointestinal illness, which is an extraintestinal vibriosis rather than the disease entity cholera. VPD not satisfied -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 42-year-old female post-gastric bypass presenting with cholecystitis and bacteremia

step5_concept_grounding: Non-O1/non-O139 Vibrio cholerae cholecystitis and bacteremia; stool cultures negative; not epidemic cholera

evidence_items.source_quote: The isolate was confirmed as   V. cholerae   by MALDI-TOF using the VITEK MS (bioMerieux, France) and then later by the Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Atlanta, GA) as a member of the nontoxigenic serotype (non-O1, non-O139). The ctxA toxigenic marker was negative by multiplex PCR.
evidence_items.test_name: CDC reference identification and multiplex PCR
evidence_items.target_concept: Nontoxigenic non-O1, non-O139 V. cholerae (ctxA negative)

evidence_items.source_quote: Stool cultures on antibiotics were negative including on   Vibrio   sp. selective media.
evidence_items.test_name: Stool culture on selective Vibrio media

rationale: A 42-year-old female with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass presented with acute cholecystitis. Blood cultures isolated non-toxigenic non-O1/non-O139 Vibrio cholerae (ctxA negative), and stool cultures were negative on selective Vibrio media. The patient suffered bacteremia and biliary tract infection due to non-O1/non-O139 Vibrio, not cholera. VPD not satisfied -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.
